title: Evidence Standard for a Vehicle with a Pattern of Fault Reports
content:
Where a Keyturn Vehicle Listing carries fault reports of its own, the evidence figure the marketplace works from on a fresh fault report is read off the pattern those reports make. Two things are counted: the fault reports standing on the vehicle's condition record in the rolling twelve months counted back from the handling date, and how many of those are a tyre tread or a brake wear fault.

| Fault reports in the rolling twelve months | Tyre tread or brake wear among them | Evidence figure taken |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3 or more | at least 1 | 10 photographs, in place of the standard evidence figure |
| 3 or more | none | 8 photographs, in place of the standard evidence figure |
| fewer than 3 | at least 1 | 6 photographs, in place of the standard evidence figure |
| any other case | — | the standard evidence figure |

Written out as clauses: a vehicle carrying three or more fault reports in the rolling twelve months counted back from the handling date, at least one of them a tyre tread or brake wear fault, takes 10 photographs in place of the standard evidence figure; one carrying three or more such reports with no tyre tread or brake wear fault among them takes 8; one carrying fewer than three fault reports in that window with at least one tyre tread or brake wear fault among them takes 6; and any other vehicle takes the standard evidence figure.

### Both sides of the count of 3

A vehicle whose condition record shows 3 fault reports inside the window, one of them a worn tyre, is on the first row and takes 10 photographs. The same vehicle showing 2 fault reports inside the window, one of them a worn tyre, is on the third row and takes 6. A vehicle showing 3 fault reports inside the window, none of them a tyre tread or brake wear fault, is on the second row and takes 8; one showing 2 such reports, neither of them a tyre tread or brake wear fault, falls to the last row.

The count runs on the rolling twelve months counted back from the handling date, so a fault report dated thirteen months back is outside the window and is not counted at all.
